_about: The crew journal's phrases (docs/samples-lab-journal.md §7), first person and short. Each event has a few variants; the game picks one by the sol, so the same day reads the same. {title} {what} {where} {count} are filled in. once: an event written once a sol at most.

lines: We're down. The lander's quiet now, and outside it's nothing but {where} in every direction.
Touchdown. I keep looking out of the port at {where}: it's ours now.
Landed. The cargo's out there waiting, and the ground is the colour of rust.
First walk outside. The suit's heavy, the sky's butterscotch, and the silence is total.
Stepped out for the first time today. My footprints are the only ones for a very long way.
Out of the airlock at last. I stood there for a minute just looking.
The fabricator finished the {what}.
One more thing made here, not shipped: the {what}.
Printed the {what} today. It still smells of warm polymer.
{title}. A good day.
{title}. One less thing Earth has to send us.
{title}. I wrote it twice to be sure.
We're self-sufficient: water, air and food, all made here. Mission Control went quiet for a while, then cheered.
{title}.
Worked on the soil: {title}.
The emergency lander came down. I'm grateful, and a little embarrassed.
Out collecting today: {what} from {where}.
Spent the afternoon sampling {where}. Bagged {what}.
The case is filling up: {what}, from {where}.
Took a sample inside {where}. The lamp makes everything look like the inside of a mine.
Sampled {where} by lamplight. No wind in here, no dust, nothing moving.
A lead in the lab: {title}. I'll need more samples from other spots.
The lab thinks it's seeing something: {title}. Not proof yet.
Confirmed today: {what}. Sent it to Earth.
We found something: {what}. I keep rereading the result.
A real discovery: {what}. Logged it for Mission Control.
Earth wrote back: {title}.
A reply from home ({title}). It's good to know someone's reading.
{title}, from Mission Control.
Earth sent a new plan today: {what}.
